cities.base: Southeast guesthouse area, quieter and cheaper, 15-20 minutes from the airport for the flight home.
cities.name: Blue Bay / Mahebourg

places.name: Piton Savanne / Gorges Panoramic Stop
places.note: Another pull-off along the same road as the main gorges viewpoints, less crowded, similar view down toward the west coast. Only add if the light is good and you have time to spare on the drive back.

places.name: Macchabee Trail
places.note: Trailhead at Macchabee car park, roughly 10km round trip through native forest to Macchabee viewpoint and back, 3-4 hours, modest elevation change under 200m. Not part of this itinerary's day trip pacing but the option if you ever swap the rum tasting for a hike.

places.name: Macchabee Viewpoint
places.note: Quieter viewpoint than Alexandra Falls, same gorge system, fewer tour buses. Starting point for the longer Macchabee Trail if you had more time than this itinerary allows.

places.name: Black River Gorges Viewpoint (Alexandra Falls)
places.note: Roadside pull-off looking down over forested gorge to the coast. No entry gate, no facilities. Late afternoon light is best, can be windy and cool up here compared to the coast.

places.name: Rhumerie de Chamarel
places.note: Working distillery with a short tour and a proper tasting flight of flavoured and aged rums. Skip the attached restaurant, overpriced and mediocre for what it charges.

places.name: Chamarel Waterfall
places.note: Single-drop 100m waterfall visible from a roadside viewpoint, no hike required. Photo stop rather than a destination, five minutes is enough unless the light is good.

places.name: Chamarel Seven Coloured Earths
places.note: Dunes of eroded volcanic rock in seven distinct colours that don't wash together even in heavy rain. Touristy, small, but a genuine geological oddity worth the short stop.

places.name: Black River Peak Trailhead
places.note: Trailhead for the hike up Mauritius's highest peak, round trip roughly 3 hours. Skip it on this itinerary, it doesn't fit the day trip's timing alongside the coloured earths and distillery, better suited to a dedicated hiking day this trip doesn't have.

places.name: Alexandra Falls Viewpoint
places.note: Roadside pull-off with a view down over the gorge and, on clear days, to the south coast. No gate, no ticket. Best light is late afternoon.

places.name: Rhumerie de Chamarel
places.note: Working sugarcane distillery, the tour and tasting flight is worth the hour. Skip the attached restaurant, overpriced and mediocre for what it is.

places.name: Chamarel Waterfall
places.note: 100m single-drop waterfall visible from a fixed viewpoint just off the road, you don't hike to its base. Five minutes at the platform is really all it takes, worth the stop since it's on the same road as the coloured earths.

places.name: Chamarel Seven Coloured Earths
places.note: Small dunes of naturally banded volcanic soil that don't erode into each other, genuinely odd geology. Gift shop sprawl around it is skippable, the viewing platform itself takes 30-45 minutes including the short loop trail.

places.name: Le Jardin de Beau Vallon
places.note: Table d'hote lunch spot on a family property near Mahebourg, home-style Mauritian Creole cooking, book ahead since it's set menu and limited seatings. Better food than anything on the main strip.

places.name: Crystal Rock Snorkel Stop
places.note: A striking rock formation rising out of open water, reachable only as a stop on the Benitiers catamaran route, not a separate booking. The best reason to pick this specific itinerary over a generic lagoon cruise.

places.name: Underwater sea walk near Ile aux Benitiers
places.note: A helmet dive walk on the lagoon floor, sold as a separate booking from some of the same operators in Tamarin. Interesting once but pricey add-on for a day that already includes Crystal Rock snorkeling.

places.name: Jet ski add-on near Ile aux Benitiers
places.note: Some operators upsell jet ski loops around the lagoon. Noisy, overpriced for 15-20 minutes, and out of place on a snorkel-focused day, better to say no.

places.name: Ile aux Benitiers fishing village
places.note: A small cluster of homes on the island, some tours mention it but most boats don't actually stop to walk through it. Not a real attraction, just visible from the beach stop.

places.name: Rum punch and music stop on the return sail
places.note: Standard end to the catamaran day, sega music and rum punch on the sail back into Tamarin around 3-4pm. Fun if you're in the mood, skippable if you'd rather nap on the deck.

places.name: Le Morne Brabant viewpoint from the water
places.note: Some catamaran routes swing past the base of Le Morne mountain, a UNESCO site tied to the history of runaway slaves. Seen from the boat only on this itinerary, not climbed.

places.name: Tamarin dolphin watching trip
places.note: 6am start, boats chase pods of spinner dolphins just offshore. Hit or miss, and multiple boats crowding the same pod feels bad. Worth skipping unless you really want it.

places.name: On-board beach BBQ lunch
places.note: Included in most catamaran packages, grilled fish, chicken, rum punch, served on the beach or on board. Quality varies a lot by operator, ask what's included before booking.

places.name: Casela Nature Parks
places.note: Marketed as an adventure park with lion walks and zip lines but functions as a zoo. Worth it only if traveling with kids who need a change of pace from the beach, otherwise skip.

places.name: Sandbank swim stop (Ile aux Benitiers lagoon)
places.note: Standing in waist-deep water in the middle of the lagoon, a standard photo stop on most catamaran itineraries, skip if you've already done this at Blue Bay or elsewhere and want more snorkel time instead.

places.name: Ile aux Benitiers lagoon reef snorkel stop
places.note: Calmer, shallower snorkeling than Crystal Rock, decent for less confident swimmers or kids, fish life is modest compared to the rock stop.

places.name: Crystal Rock
places.note: A limestone stack rising out of open water, a short snorkel stop on the catamaran route. The actual reason to book this specific trip over a generic lagoon cruise, the rock formation and drop-off are unlike the shallow lagoon snorkeling elsewhere.

places.name: Catamaran departure point, Tamarin
places.note: Most day trips to the island leave from here around 9am. Book directly with a small operator (Isla Marine, Yacht Evasion type outfits) rather than through the resort desk, same boat costs 30 percent more that way.

places.name: Black River (Riviere Noire) fishing village
places.note: Small working fishing harbour on the drive between Flic en Flac and Chamarel. Nothing to do beyond a quick look at the boats, not worth a special trip but fine if passing through.

places.name: Restaurant Le Bougainville
places.note: Waterfront seafood spot in Mahebourg, grilled fish and Mauritian curries. Straightforward and reliable rather than exciting, good option after the market.

places.name: Blue Bay shore snorkeling (public access point)
places.note: You can wade in and snorkel straight off the public beach without a boat, coral isn't as good as the boat-accessed reef but there's no cost and no schedule. Bring your own gear.

places.name: Frederik Hendrik Museum
places.note: Small archaeology museum on the Dutch landing site, VOC-era artifacts. Only for people who actually want the colonial history detail, most visitors will get more out of Mahebourg's museum.

places.name: Pointe Jerome fishing village
places.note: Where the Ile aux Aigrettes boats leave from, a working cluster of pirogues rather than a sight in itself. Worth the twenty minutes waiting for your boat, nothing to seek out beyond that.

places.name: Vieux Grand Port ruins
places.note: Foundations marking the first Dutch landing site on Mauritius in 1598. Genuinely minor, a few interpretive signs and low walls, only worth the stop if you're already driving past.

places.name: Blue Bay Public Beach
places.note: Sheltered white sand beach with filao trees for shade, calm swimming, less developed than the resort beaches up the west coast. Good for the transfer afternoon before the boat trip.

places.name: Mahebourg National History Museum (Chateau Robillard)
places.note: Small colonial-era house museum covering the 1810 Battle of Grand Port, the only French naval win in the Napoleonic wars. Worth it on a rainy afternoon, skippable otherwise.

places.name: Mahebourg Waterfront
places.note: Quiet stretch along the bay near the market, fishing boats, not built for tourists which is the point. Nothing to do here beyond a walk, pair it with the market.

places.name: Mahebourg Market
places.note: Best on Mondays, that's when the stalls actually fill out. Produce, spices, cheap clothes, not a souvenir market. An hour covers it, good for a cheap lunch off one of the food stalls.

places.name: Blue Bay Marine Park
places.note: Marine protected area with coral visible through clear shallow water, free to enter but glass-bottom boat or snorkel gear rental costs extra. Go before the wind picks up midday, visibility drops fast after 11am.

places.name: Ile aux Aigrettes
places.note: Boat out to a coral islet nature reserve run by the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation, guided walk among pink pigeons and Aldabra tortoises. Genuinely worth it, better than most people expect, book ahead as group sizes are capped.

places.name: Mahebourg market
places.note: Best on Mondays, a cheap lunch stop rather than a shopping destination.

places.name: Blue Bay Marine Park
places.note: Entry is free, glass-bottom boat or gear rental runs $15-25, best visibility before the wind picks up.

places.name: Ile aux Aigrettes nature reserve
places.note: Native tortoises and birds you won't see anywhere else on the island, better than most people expect.

places.name: Crystal Rock snorkel stop
places.note: Part of the catamaran day, not a separate booking, the reason to pick this trip over a generic cruise.

places.name: Ile aux Bénitiers catamaran trip
places.note: Book direct with an operator, not through the resort, same trip costs 30% more that way.

places.name: Alexandra Falls / Gorges Viewpoint
places.note: Free pull-off stops, go late afternoon for the light.

places.name: Chamarel rum distillery
places.note: Skip the restaurant attached, overpriced for what it is.

places.name: Chamarel Seven Coloured Earths
places.note: Touristy but genuinely strange geology, worth it once.

places.name: St Anne Church, Chamarel
places.note: Small village church, simple and unremarkable but a quick free stop if you're already parked in the village for lunch or the market stalls.

places.name: Chamarel Corn Fields Scenic Stretch
places.note: Quiet stretch of road through cultivated fields and forest just outside the village, good for stretching legs between stops, nothing to plan around specifically.

places.name: La Vallée des Couleurs Nature Park
places.note: A second, less impressive set of coloured earths bundled with zip lines and quad bikes. Skip it, you've already seen the real thing at the original Seven Coloured Earths and this adds a detour without adding much.

places.name: Chamarel village market stalls
places.note: Small run of souvenir and spice stalls along the main road. Fine to glance at while passing but not worth a dedicated stop, same goods as everywhere else on the island.

places.name: Le Chamarel Restaurant
places.note: Sit-down lunch spot on the hillside with a genuine view over the west coast, good for the midday break between the coloured earths and the gorge viewpoints. Book ahead, tour groups fill it fast.

places.name: Plaine Champagne Panorama
places.note: Open stretch of road across the plateau with wide views toward the west coast, easy to combine with the gorge stops since it's on the way.

places.name: Gorges Viewpoint (Black River Gorges National Park)
places.note: A second lookout further along the same road, deep green gorge views over native forest. Trailheads for longer hikes into the park start near here if you ever wanted more than a drive-by.

outings.why: Seven Coloured Earths, the waterfall, a rum tasting at the Chamarel distillery, and the gorge viewpoints on the way back, door to door 6-7 hours with stops.
outings.name: Chamarel and Black River Gorges
outings.season: year-round, best avoided during cyclone risk Jan-Mar
outings.fallback: Skip the gorge viewpoints and just do the Coloured Earths and distillery if time runs short.

outings.why: Full day, roughly 9am-4pm, snorkeling stops at Crystal Rock plus a beach lunch on board, the reason to pick this trip over a generic lagoon cruise.
outings.name: Catamaran to Ile aux Bénitiers and Crystal Rock
outings.season: May-November for best visibility, risk of cancellation Jan-M
outings.fallback: A shorter lagoon cruise without the Crystal Rock stop if seas are rough.

outings.why: 6am start, hit or miss on dolphins, honestly skippable and the ethics of some operators are questionable.
outings.name: Tamarin dolphin watching
outings.fallback: Sleep in and stay on the beach instead.

outings.why: Guided walk 2-2.5 hours by boat from Pointe Jerome, native tortoises and birds you won't see elsewhere on the island.
outings.name: Ile aux Aigrettes nature reserve

outings.why: Snorkeling or glass-bottom boat in the marine park, best visibility in the morning before the wind picks up.
outings.name: Blue Bay Marine Park snorkeling
outings.fallback: Glass-bottom boat instead of snorkeling if conditions are choppy.

destination.name: Mauritius
destination.pitch: A week of lagoon and reef, not culture or nightlife, and the flights alone eat two of your seven days.
destination.caveat: You're burning close to two full days of a seven-day trip just in transit and jet lag recovery, so real usable time is closer to five days. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Cheap, good dholl puri and roti at the Mahebourg market, not a fine-dining destination.
because.nature: Native tortoises and birds on Ile aux Aigrettes you won't see anywhere else on the island.
because.adventure: A full day catamaran out to Ile aux Bénitiers and Crystal Rock for snorkeling.
because.relaxation: Calm lagoon swimming before breakfast at Flic en Flac and sunsets that land right over the sea.
because.exploration: The Seven Coloured Earths and Black River Gorges viewpoints make for one strange, worthwhile inland day.
